- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near-zero and recent prices are falling — model fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes, especially when sentiment >0.4 and price is rising — forecast peaks too early.
- When sentiment is low (0.0–0.2) and price is trending down, model often fails to fully correct — underestimates drop depth.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates after strong upward moves, underestimates after strong downward moves — adjust for recent trend reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive — correct by reducing initial forecast by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits to recent sentiment — dampen forecast sensitivity to sentiment changes.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.0–0.1) over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid false optimism.
